title: Yemen Desk
subtitle: The daily brief on the campaign against the Houthis

editions.lede: The fight is widening from airports into an open exchange over oil and fuel.

items.headline: Coalition strikes Houthi fuel sites; Houthis threaten Saudi oil
items.text: The Saudi-led coalition struck Houthi-held energy sites, including the Al Sabahah fuel station in Sanaa and fuel-loading piers at Hodeidah. The Houthis answered by declaring Saudi oil installations legitimate targets and telling workers to stay away.

items.headline: Government claims new ground in Marib
items.text: Under the Dawn of Yemen operation, government forces claim the heights around Maas camp in Medghal, in the northwest, and al-Muqailat and Jabal Zajjar north of Harib. Some Yemeni outlets say Maas camp itself fell; Al Jazeera reported only the surrounding heights. Independent confirmation of the camp is thin.

items.headline: Fighting continues west of Taiz
items.text: Fighting continues on the western approaches, at al-Dhabab and nearby. Government sources claim dozens of Houthi fighters were captured at al-Dhabab. Al-Waziiya remains the choke point toward the Mocha coast.

items.headline: Three missiles intercepted; Riyadh airport still closed
items.text: The coalition says it intercepted three missiles aimed at Riyadh and Khamis Mushait. King Khalid airport in Riyadh is still closed through 17 October; streets and offices there are otherwise reported as normal.

editions.trend: The clearest government ground claims so far are in Marib rather than on the Red Sea coast.
editions.watch: Whether any Saudi Aramco or pipeline site is actually hit after the Houthi oil threat.

editions.lede: Saudi air defenses are under strain, and the Houthis are pressing the government's supply roads on the ground.

items.headline: Saudi air defenses under strain
items.text: Officials told AP that the kingdom is investigating how Saturday's barrage reached Riyadh; drones were sent ahead of cruise and ballistic missiles. The Wall Street Journal reports that interceptors are running low and batteries are being moved to protect energy sites and palaces. Riyadh airport stays closed until 17 October. The coalition says it intercepted missiles aimed at Riyadh and Khamis Mushait on Monday night; Yahya Saree claims a hit on the airport.

items.headline: Saudi agencies raise readiness
items.text: The information minister said all state agencies have raised their readiness, that life continues normally, and that citizens should not share unofficial footage.

items.headline: Trump speaks with the Crown Prince; no decision
items.text: President Trump spoke with the Crown Prince on Monday and said the Houthis are "misbehaving very badly," but announced no decision. Iran offered to help start Saudi-Houthi talks; no Saudi reply is reported. Haaretz reports that the Crown Prince refused an Israeli request to join the campaign.

items.headline: Fighting reaches al-Dhabab, the entrance to Taiz
items.text: The fighting is now at al-Dhabab, the city's southwestern entrance. Government military reports say the Houthis can fire on the al-Dhabab road. Government forces say they retook several hills there. The Houthis have not commented.

items.headline: Houthi attack in Lahj toward the coast road
items.text: Government-aligned media say the Houthis are attacking in al-Madaraba toward the coast road that supplies the Bab al-Mandab front.

editions.trend: The Houthis are attacking the roads that supply both Taiz and the Bab al-Mandab front, while Saudi Arabia is reported to be short of interceptors.
editions.watch: The Southern Transitional Council's mass rally in Aden on 14 October, called by Aidarous al-Zubaidi as a mobilization against the Houthis.

editions.lede: Riyadh airport was hit again on Sunday, and the Houthis now openly claim the attacks.

items.headline: Riyadh airport struck again
items.text: A projectile struck Terminal 4 at King Khalid airport on 11 October and started a fire. The civil aviation authority says one person was killed and eleven were wounded. The airport remains closed. Saturday's death toll has risen to 13 after an Indian citizen died of his wounds.

items.headline: Houthis claim the strikes; Saudi defenses intercept more
items.text: Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree claimed Saturday's strike, and also claimed hits on Dammam airport and two Aramco facilities. Saudi Arabia and Aramco have not confirmed the Aramco claim. The coalition reports intercepting a cruise missile near Riyadh, a drone over the Eastern Province and a ballistic missile aimed at Khamis Mushait. Civil defense alerts sounded in Abha.

items.headline: Riyadh conferences will go ahead
items.text: Reuters reports that organizers say the major Riyadh conferences, including the Future Investment Initiative on 26 to 29 October, will go ahead.

items.headline: New attack at al-Wazi'iyah, west of Taiz
items.text: The Giants Brigades and Nation's Shield say they opened a new attack at al-Wazi'iyah and repelled a Houthi push toward Dhubab airport. The Houthis have not commented. The government says the main roads into Taiz are open, but its own health ministry describes the siege as tightening. Government sources say aircraft are now targeting Houthi supply routes around the city.

editions.trend: The Houthis are doing steady damage to the Saudi home front, while government ground gains have slowed to holding the Bab al-Mandab area.
editions.watch: Whether President Trump decides to join the strikes. On Saturday he said, "We may."
